summary.title: SPEC CPU2026: Characterization, Representativeness, and Cross-Suite Comparison
summary.one_liner: SPEC CPU2026 is a more frontend-heavy, larger-footprint general-purpose CPU benchmark than SPEC CPU2017, and its profile closely resembles CPU-centric agentic AI workloads.
keywords: is spec cpu2026 good for agentic ai
how does spec cpu2026 differ from spec cpu2017
takeaways: SPEC CPU2026 increases instruction volume, memory footprint, and instruction-cache stress compared with SPEC CPU2017.
It is closer to datacenter-like frontend pressure than prior CPU generations, but less vector-intensive than MLPerf and less frontend-extreme than DCPerf.
An agentic AI pipeline's features fall within SPEC CPU2026's behavioral spread, suggesting it as a proxy for CPU-centric agentic workloads.
Case studies cover page sizes and allocators, prefetching, compilers, ISA sensitivity, many-core scaling, and new rolling round-robin (RRR) runs.
summary.summary: The paper characterizes SPEC CPU2026 on nine recent Intel, AMD, Ampere, and Nvidia platforms using microarchitectural metrics. It compares the suite with SPEC CPU2017, DCPerf, MLPerf, and agentic AI probes to show where each suite resembles or differs from the others. The authors conclude SPEC CPU2026 remains a complementary general-purpose suite with a broader frontend envelope that matches agentic AI behavior. Case studies on page sizes, allocators, prefetching, compilers, ISA, many-core scaling, and RRR runs illustrate its use beyond aggregate scores. The page text is an arXiv abstract listing, so detailed results are not included.
